deep_dive.title: Synergy-Aware Residual Flow Matching for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
deep_dive.abstract: Predicting single-cell responses to genetic and chemical perturbations is important for understanding regulatory mechanisms and prioritizing therapeutic interventions. Existing methods have made progress by modeling perturbation-conditioned expression shifts with neural networks, graph priors, foundation-model representations, or distributional generative models. However, combinatorial perturbation prediction remains challenging because much of the response can be explained by additive single-perturbation effects, while the biologically informative signal often lies in a smaller non-additive residual induced by perturbation interactions. Directly generating the full post-perturbation expression profile may therefore allocate substantial capacity to the dominant additive component and underemphasize synergy-specific structure. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{SynGeneFlow}, a synergy-aware flow matching framework that anchors the source distribution at an additive prior and learns a residual flow toward the true perturbed state. SynGeneFlow further incorporates perturbation-conditioned gene interaction modeling, where a static gene-gene mask provides biological structure and a perturbation-dependent deformation bias dynamically modulates gene-gene coupling. To preserve population-level response structure, we align both endpoint distributions and biological residual distributions with MMD-based regularization. We evaluate SynGeneFlow on genetic and drug perturbation benchmarks under observed-single, held-out, and cross-modality settings. The results demonstrate that residualizing flow matching around additive perturbation effects provides a biologically grounded and robust framework for single-cell perturbation response prediction.

deep_dive.title: A Pitfall in the Evaluation of Gene Perturbation Models
deep_dive.abstract: Gene perturbation models aim to predict transcriptional responses to unseen genetic interventions, but comparisons rely on heterogeneous evaluation metrics and differentially-expressed (DE) gene subsets. We investigate the consequences of these choices using eight methods across six single-gene perturbation datasets under a unified evaluation protocol. Varying the number of top DE genes reveals substantial instability in Precision-based rankings, with the winning method changing $86.7\%$ of the time, while rankings based on the rest of the metrics remain comparatively stable. Investigating this discrepancy exposes that repeating a single predicted expression profile across cell-level rows, a standard practice for many methods, can inflate significance estimates and produce excessively large predicted significant-DE sets. Specifically we found that $67.1\%$ of tested perturbation--gene pairs pass the significance threshold despite some of them having minuscule effects. We derive an inflation factor showing that replicated predictions can amplify the standardized Mann--Whitney statistic even after correction for tied ranks, without adding independent information. This artifact changes Precision mainly as the number of DE genes increases because for smaller cutoffs, most of the genes are already significant due to the effect-based ordering. Taking this pitfall into account in our benchmark comparison, we find that a random forest using Gene Ontology features achieves the best overall results.

This work unifies evaluation across eight methods and six datasets, revealing that DE-gene choices drastically change rankings and that repeating predicted profiles inflates significance.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 基因扰动模型旨在预测细胞对未见遗传干预的转录响应，但现有比较依赖异质指标与差异表达基因子集。作者在统一评估协议下用八种方法、六个单基因扰动数据集系统考察评估选择的影响。结果显示，改变差异表达基因数目会使基于精度的排名剧烈波动，获胜方法高达86.7%的情况下发生改变，而重复使用单一预测表达谱会夸大显著性估计。该工作揭示了扰动响应预测评估中的关键陷阱，对虚拟细胞模型的可靠比较具有重要意义。

quick_skim.title: Panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes at scale with CellNet
quick_skim.abstract: Comprehensively characterizing cellular diversity is critical for understanding tissue development, identifying disease-associated populations and investigating gene programmes linked to specialized functions. Advances in single-cell profiling reveal additional cell-specific transcripts and molecular associations, yet many foundation models represent only a restricted portion of this increasingly rich molecular information. Here we present CellNet, which enables panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes by integrating DNA-derived gene identities and measured RNA expression in a shared image representation. Pretrained on 231 million cell profiles spanning 40 species, CellNet improves rare-population and condition-associated state recognition in evaluated cohorts while retaining competitive general cell representations. It predicts withheld coding-gene expression and selected non-coding targets in total-RNA data, and recovers lineage-specific expression patterns in spatial measurements. Prediction also extends across species, including to targets without expression-pretraining exposure. Its gene representations retrieve known non-coding modules and developmental or neural programmes, including from sparsely detected RNA queries. Together, these results establish CellNet as a scalable framework for interpreting cellular diversity through increasingly comprehensive transcriptomic measurements.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: large-scale single-cell transcriptome foundation model, a backbone for virtual cell modeling

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 单细胞测序揭示了丰富的细胞特异性转录本与分子关联，但现有基础模型仅能表征其中有限部分，限制了细胞多样性的刻画。作者提出CellNet，将DNA来源的基因身份与实测RNA表达整合到共享的图像表示中，并在跨40个物种的2.31亿细胞谱上预训练。模型提升了稀有细胞群和条件相关状态的识别能力。该全景式单细胞建模为构建虚拟细胞提供了更强的表征基础，但未直接涉及扰动响应预测。
